URL: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/politics/2026/09/25/angela-rayner-attack-shabana-mahmood-migrant-crackdown/
Telegraph — published 25 September 2026 9:40pm BST (21:40 BST Fri). By Charles Hymas, Home Affairs Editor.

HEADLINE: Angela Rayner attacks Shabana Mahmood's migrant crackdown
Standfirst: Communities Secretary says proposals affecting care workers who 'moved their lives here' are unfair

Angela Rayner has attacked Shabana Mahmood's migrant crackdown on the eve of the Labour Party conference. Rayner said the Home Secretary's plans to make it harder for migrant workers to claim settlement were unfair because they would "change the goalposts". She said the plans would hit foreign care workers who had "moved their lives here to look after our loved ones". They face being forced to wait up to 15 years before they can claim indefinite leave to remain (ILR), as opposed to the current five years.

FACTS:
- Rayner, the Communities Secretary, "made clear that she had not changed her critical views of the proposals since she was brought back into government by Andy Burnham. On the back benches, she described the retrospective nature of the proposals as 'un-British'."
- "The Prime Minister has indicated that he is rethinking the plans, which he also criticised before taking up the post, and has hinted that an exemption for foreign care workers is on the table."
- "Ms Rayner's comments threaten to ignite a public row over the issue at the Labour conference, which opens on Sunday in Liverpool. Some 100 Labour MPs have signed a letter criticising the proposals and calling for exemptions for foreign care workers."
- "The Telegraph reported that Britain's biggest trade union, Unison, is planning a demonstration outside the conference on Monday to support moves to exempt care workers from the ILR changes."
- Recruitment of foreign care workers surged in 2022 when the Tory government opened up a health and social care visa route.
- The relaxation of UK visa rules by Boris Johnson - the so-called Boriswave - "saw 4.2 million migrants come to the UK between 2021 and 2024, peaking at 944,000 in the year to March 2023."
- "Last year, Ms Mahmood's predecessor Yvette Cooper changed the rules to end the recruitment of care workers from abroad, in an attempt to curb net migration. The Tories had also banned care workers from bringing family dependents with them."
- Mahmood said this week the Government would make a decision on the policy "very soon".

QUOTE (Angela Rayner, Communities Secretary, to The Times, asked whether she stood by her views before she came into government):
"Especially in regards to the carers, who were asked to come to this country to care for some of our most vulnerable and then we changed the goalposts years down the line, I think that's very disruptive."

QUOTE (Angela Rayner):
"I do have concerns about that... when you ask someone to come here and look after your most vulnerable and they spend years dedicating themselves, moving their lives here to look after our loved ones."

QUOTE (Angela Rayner, asked whether she had raised the issue with Mahmood directly):
"I think Shabana knows. It was in the newspaper at the time. I've not changed my view on that. I just think when people relocate because we have skills shortages in this country, I think we have to be aware of that."

QUOTE (Shabana Mahmood, Home Secretary, to the home affairs select committee this week):
"I accept that there are a lot of people wondering what rules will apply to them. It is right that the Government has taken time to look at consultation responses properly."

QUOTE (Shabana Mahmood):
"I can assure people we are trying to do a proper piece of work, where we have the right arrangements that strike the right balance between our responsibilities to people who have come here to work, our recognition of the failures we inherited as a government and also our need to do right by the people who are already here and who pay for the systems that we all rely on."

SECOND APPROVED SOURCE (originating interview): The Times — https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/angela-rayner-visa-crackdown-care-workers-gcqxpmlcr ("Rayner condemns Labour's migrant visa crackdown"). Also The Times: https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/angela-rayner-housing-hmrc-tax-immigration-vzl2kflfq ("I've not spoken to Starmer in quite a while, says Rayner"). Sky News's Saturday front-pages round-up confirms The Times splash: "Angela Rayner has told The Times she disagrees with the home secretary's plan to make it harder for foreign care workers to get permanent residency in the UK."
